submission.justification: Simulations at 30% coverage (100k events each): D3 = 54.0 PE/MeV, D2 = 37.4, D1 = 24.9. This matches the 2025 summary (light rises with coverage, about coverage^0.8), so D3 at the maximum allowed coverage gives the most light. Feedthroughs support 30% coverage, and the cold electronics have been validated for all designs. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: none of the project documents have any thermal-cycling or failure-rate data for any design. That means the hard requirement (no more than 5% of modules failing after 20 cycles from 300 K to 87 K) is UNVERIFIED for all three options. D3 has an extra specific risk: its thin bonded dichroic filter could delaminate because of thermal-expansion mismatch. This recommendation is CONDITIONAL. Before the Q3 design freeze, D3 must pass a 20-cycle qualification on a statistically meaningful sample, with an upper bound on the failure rate of 5% or less. If D3 fails, fall back to D2 at 30% (37.4 PE/MeV), provided D2 passes the same test. Then use D1 if needed. Modules cannot be replaced, so the design should not be frozen until this test is done.

requirements.evidence: At 30% coverage, D3 gives 53.99 PE/MeV, compared with 37.37 for D2 and 24.86 for D1. Light increases with coverage, so 30% (the maximum) is best.
